claims.shortExcerpt: Laurus nobilis — identity from Royal Horticultural Society.
Common / synonym names for Bay Laurel.

RHS: 'Generally hardy to -5°C (23°F) but can withstand lower temperatures in sheltered positions' and frost can damage foliage; NCSU: 'needs to be brought indoors in the winter in areas colder than zone 8b to prevent frost damage' (USDA 8b–10b).
claims.transformation: Mapped RHS ground hardiness ~-5°C + NCSU zone 8b frost-damage threshold to qualitative frostSensitivity=medium (neither frost-intolerant tropical nor fully frost-hardy temperate).

claims.shortExcerpt: RHS generally hardy to -5°C; NCSU USDA Plant Hardiness Zone 8b–10b; colder than 8b requires winter protection.
No explicit heat-tolerance rating found in consulted RHS/NCSU pages; Mediterranean native range retained as provisional heuristic.
claims.enrichmentReason: Authoritative sources do not publish a direct heatTolerance label.

claims.shortExcerpt: NCSU/RHS pages do not state an atmospheric RH mortality or humidity-tolerance class; Mediterranean origin alone is insufficient for SOURCE_SUPPORTED humidityTolerance.
RHS: water container-grown bay moderately; over-watering can cause root damage. NCSU Soil Drainage: Good Drainage; Occasionally Dry.
claims.transformation: Moderate watering + avoid waterlogging / occasionally dry → waterNeeds=low (drought-tolerant once established; not high-moisture).

claims.shortExcerpt: RHS Aspect: Full sun or partial shade. NCSU Light: Full sun (6 or more hours) / Partial Shade.
claims.transformation: Canonical sunNeeds=full_sun as primary recommendation; partial shade also acceptable per sources.

claims.shortExcerpt: RHS: 'Bay needs a well-drained soil'. NCSU: Soil Drainage Good Drainage; leaf spots often caused by waterlogged roots.
Evergreen Mediterranean shrub; sources describe frost protection needs, not a temperate winter-chill hour requirement for flowering.
claims.transformation: Absence of chill-hour requirement in RHS/NCSU guidance + evergreen Mediterranean habit → needsWinterChill=false.

claims.value: Bay Laurel (Laurus nobilis). Mediterranean evergreen; culinary foliage.
claims.shortExcerpt: Mediterranean evergreen; culinary foliage

claims.value: Small greenish-yellow male or female flowers in spring (RHS); NCSU: green/white/yellow flowers March–May on dioecious trees.
claims.shortExcerpt: RHS: Small greenish-yellow male or female flowers are produced in spring. NCSU: Dioecious; flowers appear in the spring from March to May.

claims.value: Black/purple drupes form on female plants after pollination; not a culinary fruit crop requirement for leaf use.
claims.shortExcerpt: RHS: flowers followed by black berries on female plants. NCSU: only female plants produce fleshy black/purple drupes.
Hardiness — Generally hardy to -5°C (23°F) but can withstand lower temperatures in sheltered positions. Bay is hardier when planted in the ground.
claims.transformation: Stored RHS published general hardiness figure as minimum_survival_temperature_c=-5. Not an absolute extreme-event authority.

claims.shortExcerpt: NCSU: 'It has separate male and female plants (i.e., it is dioecious), with only the female ones producing the fleshy, black drupes.' RHS: male or female flowers; black berries on female plants.
Dioecious; fruit forms on female plants only — pollen from a male plant is required for seeded fruit set.
claims.transformation: Dioecy + female-only fruit → requires_pollinator=true for fruit set (leaf harvest does not require fruit).

claims.shortExcerpt: Female plants produce berries/drupes; male or female flowers on separate plants.
Dioecious species — individual plants are not self-fertile for fruit production.
claims.transformation: Dioecy implies self_fertile=false for fruit set.
